finding.title: Untrusted input to integer conversion
finding.trigger: Passing a malicious string to argv[1]
finding.assumptions: The input to the program is controlled by an attacker.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for any path from the untrusted source (argv[1]) to a dangerous operation. The only operation involving the value of N is the integer conversion on line 63 and its subsequent use in shared memory allocation on line 13. There is no system call, exec, or shell command that uses this value, so no command injection is possible. The allocation uses N * N * sizeof(int) and the program checks for a negative shmid and exits on failure, preventing any use of a malformed size. The negative or excessively large N would simply cause the program to exit gracefully, not to execute unintended commands. Therefore, no exploit exists.

finding.title: Integer division leading to truncation
finding.assumptions: N is a large number and numProcessors is small, leading to an integer division that truncates the result.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked whether integer division could cause buffer overflows, off-by-one errors, or negative indices. Lines 80-86 show rowsPerProcessor used only to split work, with last processor adjusting endRow to N, preventing out-of-bounds access. No subsequent use of rowsPerProcessor leads to memory corruption or security-sensitive operations.

finding.title: Race condition in shared memory
finding.trigger: Multiple child processes accessing shared memory concurrently
finding.assumptions: Multiple child processes may access shared memory segments concurrently without proper synchronization.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The source of data is internal shared memory, not an untrusted external input. Even if treated as untrusted, the code reads from A and B only and writes to distinct rows of C per child process. No overlapping writes or reads occur, so no data race exists. Therefore the reported race condition is incorrect.

finding.title: Resource leak in shared memory cleanup
finding.sink: shmctl(shmidA, IPC_RMID, NULL); shmctl(shmidB, IPC_RMID, NULL); shmctl(shmidC, IPC_RMID, NULL);
finding.assumptions: If any child process fails to detach the shared memory segments, the cleanup may not occur.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1) The code explicitly calls detachMatrix(A), detachMatrix(B), detachMatrix(C) in the child process after matrix multiplication (lines 92‑94). 2) Even if a child process terminated prematurely (e.g., due to a crash or signal), the operating system automatically detaches all shared memory segments attached to that process upon exit. 3) The parent process waits for all child processes to finish before performing its own detach and removal of the shared memory segments (wait loop on line 99, detachment on lines 104‑106). Therefore, the shared memory segments are always properly detached and removed, and no resource leak can occur as described.
